The analyzed JET hybrid discharge #94875 had a toroidal magnetic field of 2.8 T, plasma current of 2.2 MA, NBI power of 27 MW, and ICRH power of 6.1 MW.

Two versions of the QuaLiKiz turbulence model were compared: 2.6.1 (used in a previous study) and the newer 2.8.2, which included improvements to the trapped electron mode dependence on collisionality and a recalibration of the ETG saturation rule.
The integrated modeling with QuaLiKiz 2.6.1 reproduced the experimental profiles well but predicted a significant role for ETG turbulence and an associated anti-GyroBohm isotope scaling.
The QuaLiKiz 2.8.2 simulations showed a reduced impact of removing ETG turbulence compared to 2.6.1, leading to a significantly diminished anti-GyroBohm isotope scaling prediction.
In QuaLiKiz 2.8.2, TEM modes were found to dominate the ion-scale spectrum at k_θρ_s ≥ 0.5, contributing to the electron heat flux, whereas in 2.6.1 the ion-scale modes were purely ITG.

The gyrokinetic analysis using the GENE code showed that multiscale simulations produced no significant ETG heat flux, contradicting the rules-of-thumb used to predict the onset of ETG turbulence in the integrated modeling.

The authors concluded that the newer QuaLiKiz 2.8.2 version shows a reduced importance of ETG turbulence compared to the previous 2.6.1 version, and that simple rules-of-thumb are insufficient criteria for predicting the onset of ETG turbulence.
The authors investigated the sensitivity of ETG turbulence predictions to impurity content by considering both a nominal case and a case with 15% reduced line-averaged Z_eff.
The improved ion heat confinement regime typical of the hybrid scenario was predicted to rely on both E×B rotation shear and electromagnetic stabilization of ITG turbulence.
The ad-hoc nature of the electromagnetic stabilization model in QuaLiKiz was identified as a caveat that requires further investigation.
The integrated modeling results were within 1σ of the experimental measurements for the bulk of the profiles, demonstrating the overall success of the QuaLiKiz model in reproducing the scenario.
The gyrokinetic analysis served as a validation of the QuaLiKiz predictions and a test of its assumptions regarding the onset and importance of ETG turbulence.

The study focused on the validation of ETG turbulence predictions, but a related work has recently been published that studies the isotope scaling predictions of this discharge more generally using integrated modeling.

The extreme computational expense of multiscale gyrokinetic simulations, typically 10^7 CPU hours for a single converged simulation, precludes extensive parameter variations for testing the rules-of-thumb robustness.
A counter-example to a literal interpretation of the rules-of-thumb for predicting the onset of significant ETG turbulence was recently shown in the analysis of dedicated JET experiments.
